examples.en: A nail sticks out from the wall.
A forehead that sticks out forward is his feature.
The rock jutted out toward the sea.
Be careful of the corner sticking out next to the door.
Part of the window was designed to protrude outward.

examples.ko: 카메라가 뒤로 돌출해서 책상에 놓으면 흔들려요.
examples.en: The camera sticks out at the back, so it wobbles on a desk.

explain: '돌출하다'는 어떤 부분이 밖으로 툭 튀어나온 모양을 말해요. 일상에서는 '튀어나오다'가 훨씬 자연스럽고, '돌출'은 설명이나 건축·의학 글에서 써요.

phrases.en: A nail is sticking out of the wall, so it's dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돌출하다'보다 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more common, everyday way to say 'stick out'.

phrases.en: Be careful not to hit the protruding part.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-된'을 붙여 물건의 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-된' lets you describe the shape of an object.

phrases.example: 이 의자는 다리가 밖으로 돌출되어 있어요.
phrases.en: This chair's legs stick out to the sides.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돌출하다'보다 상태를 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more natural than '돌출하다' when describing a state.

explain_en: 돌출하다 describes a part that sticks out from a surface. In everyday talk 튀어나오다 is much more natural, while 돌출 appears in technical, architectural, and medical writing.

examples.ko: 길이 지그재그로 나 있어서 천천히 올라갔어요.
examples.en: The road zigzags, so I climbed slowly.
I bought a zigzag-pattern T-shirt.
The mountain road zigzagged, so I felt carsick.
There is a person walking in a zigzag.
Draw the line in a zigzag shape.
The skier comes down in a zigzag.

explain: '지그재그로 걷다/운전하다/그리다'처럼 '로'와 함께 부사처럼 써요. '지그재그 무늬'처럼 명사 앞에도 와요. 이어진 곡선이 아니라 꺾이는 모양이라는 점이 '구불구불'과 달라요.

phrases.en: I walked in a zigzag along the snowy road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지그재그'를 부사처럼 써서 꺾이는 모양으로 움직인다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an adverb to say you move in a zigzag pattern.

phrases.en: I drew a line in a zigzag on the paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림이나 선의 모양을 말할 때 '로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 로 to describe the shape of a line or drawing.

phrases.en: The zigzag-patterned socks are cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 바로 붙여서 무늬 이름처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed directly before a noun, like a pattern name.

explain_en: It acts like an adverb with '로', as in '지그재그로 걷다/운전하다/그리다', and also comes before nouns, as in '지그재그 무늬'. Unlike '구불구불' (winding), it has sharp turns rather than smooth curves.

examples.ko: 상자 겉면에 주소를 크게 적어 주세요.
examples.en: Please write the address in large letters on the outside of the box.

examples.ko: 이 과일은 겉면이 매끈하고 윤기가 나요.
examples.en: The surface of this fruit is smooth and shiny.

examples.ko: 겉면만 보고 속을 판단하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't judge the inside just by the outside.
The outside of the frying pan is very hot, so be careful.
The expiration date is printed on the outside of the package.
Please bake the outside of the bread until it's golden brown.

explain: '겉'보다 좀 더 구체적으로, 상자·과일·책처럼 면이 있는 물건의 바깥쪽 면을 말할 때 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '속'이나 '안쪽'이에요. 사람의 성격처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에는 '겉면'보다 '겉'을 써요.

phrases.en: The outside surface of the book got wet in the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책의 바깥쪽 면을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the outer surface of a book.

phrases.en: The surface of this stone is rough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 바깥쪽의 느낌을 말할 때 형용사와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with adjectives to describe how an outer surface feels.

phrases.en: I wiped the outside of the fridge clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소할 때 바깥쪽만 닦는다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cleaning only the outer side.

explain_en: It is a little more specific than '겉': it fits the outer face of things that have a surface, such as boxes, fruit and books. Its opposites are '속' and '안쪽'. For things you cannot see, like a person's character, use '겉' rather than '겉면'.

t90.ax: The surface of this fruit is smooth and shiny.

en: to distinguish; to classify; to tell apart

examples.en: I sort the trash by type.
Could you tell the twins apart from the start?
I'm going to separate the items by color.
It's hard to tell the two words apart.

examples.ko: 일하는 시간과 쉬는 시간을 구분해서 지내요.
examples.en: I keep work time and rest time separate.
Please tell me slowly how to distinguish them.

explain: '구분하다'는 기준을 두고 나눌 때 써요. '구별하다'는 차이를 알아본다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 'A와 B를 구분하다', '~으로 구분하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: It's hard to tell the twins apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구분하다'가 기준으로 나누는 느낌이면, '구별하다'는 차이를 알아보는 쪽이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '구분하다' is dividing by a standard; '구별하다' focuses on noticing differences.

phrases.example: 두 색이 비슷해서 구분이 안 돼요.
phrases.en: The two colors are so similar that I can't tell them apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차이를 알 수 없을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you cannot see the difference.

phrases.example: 나이를 구분하지 않고 누구나 참가할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Anyone can join regardless of age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차별이나 나눔 없이 모두를 같게 대할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when treating everyone the same without dividing them into groups.

explain_en: 구분하다 is used when you divide things by some standard. 구별하다 leans more toward noticing the difference. It appears as 'A와 B를 구분하다' (tell A from B) or '~으로 구분하다' (divide into ~).

t90.ax: I sort the trash by type.

examples.en: The bird flapped its wings strongly and took off.
The butterfly's wing flapping looks very light.
The baby bird started clumsy flapping of its wings.
I can hear the buzzing of the bee's wings.
A hummingbird flaps its wings dozens of times a second.

examples.ko: 날갯짓 몇 번에 새는 하늘 높이 올랐어요.
examples.en: With a few flaps of its wings, the bird rose high into the sky.

explain: '날갯짓하다'처럼 동사로도 쓰고, '날개를 퍼덕이다'보다 움직임을 짧게 말하는 느낌이에요. '새로운 날갯짓을 시작하다'처럼 도전의 시작을 비유할 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: The bird flaps its wings busily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '날갯짓'을 동사로 바꾼 말로 '을/를 하다'보다 짧아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun turned into a verb, shorter than 'do a wingbeat'.

phrases.en: The bird stopped flapping and perched on a branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날갯짓이 끝나는 순간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the moment the flapping stops.

phrases.en: My eyes were drawn to the eagle's powerful wingbeats.
phrases.nuance_ko: '힘찬'을 앞에 붙이면 움직임이 강하다는 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '힘찬' before it adds a sense of strong movement.

explain_en: It can also be used as the verb '날갯짓하다', and it sounds more compact than '날개를 퍼덕이다'. It is sometimes used figuratively, as in '새로운 날갯짓을 시작하다', for starting a new challenge.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 다단계 판매로 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: That company got in trouble over multilevel sales.

examples.ko: 친구가 다단계 사업을 같이 하자고 해서 거절했어요.
examples.en: A friend asked me to join a multilevel business and I refused.
You must be careful about the multilevel method from the start.

examples.ko: 이 로켓은 다단계 구조로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This rocket has a multistage structure.

examples.ko: 다단계 업체에 돈을 맡겼다가 손해를 봤어요.
examples.en: He entrusted money to a multilevel firm and lost out.
They are selling the new product through multilevel distribution.

explain: 여러 단계로 이루어진 구조를 말하지만, 일상에서는 사람을 모아 물건을 파는 '다단계 판매'의 뜻으로 가장 많이 써요. 이때는 조심하라는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 로켓이나 과정처럼 단계가 여럿이라는 뜻으로도 쓰여요.

phrases.en: You have to be careful with multi-level marketing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다단계'만 말할 때보다 사람을 모아 물건을 파는 일이라는 뜻이 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes it clear this means selling products through recruited people.

phrases.en: That person works at a multi-level marketing company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다단계 방식으로 일하는 회사를 가리키고 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a company that works by that method, with a negative feel.

phrases.en: The spacecraft flies into the sky using a multistage rocket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 판매가 아니라 단계가 여러 개라는 원래 뜻으로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the original meaning of several stages, not selling.

explain_en: It means a structure of several stages, but in daily life it is most commonly '다단계 판매' (multilevel sales), which carries a cautionary, negative tone. It can also mean multistage things like rockets or processes.

examples.en: In winter, I crave refreshing dongchimi.
I drank a bowl of dongchimi broth.
My mother made dongchimi herself.
I eat noodles with dongchimi broth.

examples.ko: 동치미는 너무 짜지 않게 담가야 맛있어요.
examples.en: Dongchimi tastes good when it isn't made too salty.
This restaurant is famous for its dongchimi cold noodles.

explain: 국물이 많은 물김치의 한 종류로, 겨울에 특히 많이 먹어요. 고구마나 떡과 같이 먹으면 잘 어울려요. '담그다'는 '담가요'처럼 ㅡ가 빠지는 활용이에요.

phrases.en: My mom makes dongchimi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 김치류는 '만들다'보다 '담그다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For kimchi-type foods, 'damgeuda' is used rather than 'make'.

phrases.en: I ate noodles in dongchimi broth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동치미 국물에 말아 먹는 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Noodles served in the dongchimi broth.

phrases.en: I crunched on the dongchimi radish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국물 속에 든 무를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the radish in the broth.

explain_en: It is a kind of watery kimchi with lots of broth, and people eat it especially in winter. It goes well with sweet potatoes or rice cakes. The verb '담그다' drops its ㅡ in conjugation, as in '담가요'.

examples.en: When a volcano erupts, magma rises to the surface.
Magma is deep underground.
When magma cools and hardens, it becomes rock.
The temperature of magma is over a thousand degrees.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 마그마와 용암의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class, I learned the difference between magma and lava.
He is a scholar who studies the magma underground.

explain: 땅속에 있을 때는 '마그마', 땅 위로 흘러나오면 '용암'이라고 해요. 과학 시간이나 화산 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '용암'이 더 익숙하게 들려요.

phrases.en: Hot lava flowed out of the volcano.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마그마가 땅 위로 나오면 '용암'이라고 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: Once magma comes out onto the surface, it's called lava.

phrases.en: Magma is rising from underground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화산이 터지기 전의 모습을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe what happens before a volcano erupts.

phrases.en: The temperature of the magma underground is very high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마그마가 있는 위치를 말할 때 '땅속'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '땅속' to say where magma is located.

explain_en: Underground it is '마그마', and once it flows out onto the surface it is called '용암' (lava). It comes up in science class and volcano news. In everyday talk, '용암' may sound more familiar.

examples.en: In spring, I bought tomato seedlings at the market.
I transplanted the seedlings into a pot.

examples.ko: 아버지는 텃밭에 상추 모종을 심고 계세요.
examples.en: My father is planting lettuce seedlings in the vegetable garden.

examples.ko: 모종이 시들지 않게 물을 자주 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to water often so the seedlings don't wilt.
I picked out a few seedlings at the flower shop.
The seedlings grew and bore fruit!

explain: '씨앗'은 아직 심기 전의 것이고, '모종'은 씨앗에서 싹이 터서 옮겨 심을 만큼 자란 어린 식물이에요. 보통 '모종을 사다', '모종을 심다'로 말해요. 텃밭이나 베란다 키우기에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: I planted pepper seedlings in the garden plot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옮겨 심는 일을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for transplanting.

phrases.en: I bought lettuce seedlings at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씨앗 대신 어느 정도 자란 식물을 살 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when buying a young plant instead of seeds.

phrases.en: The seedlings are growing well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심은 뒤 크는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how they grow after planting.

explain_en: A 씨앗 is a seed before planting, while a 모종 is a young plant that has already sprouted and is ready to be transplanted. People say 모종을 사다 or 모종을 심다. You hear it often in talk about home vegetable gardens.

examples.en: This bowl has a flower pattern.
They put a traditional pattern on the hanbok.

examples.ko: 벽지 문양은 눈에 띄지 않는 걸로 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked a wallpaper pattern that doesn't stand out.
The geometric design on the carpet is pretty.

examples.ko: 건물 벽에 새겨진 문양의 뜻이 궁금해요.
examples.en: I'm curious about the meaning of the design carved on the building wall.
The price changes depending on the fabric pattern.

explain: 문양은 옷, 그릇, 건물에 반복해서 들어가는 장식 모양이에요. '무늬'는 일상에서 더 흔하게 쓰고, 문양은 전통, 문화, 디자인 이야기에서 더 자주 써요. 옷의 줄무늬는 '줄 문양'보다 '줄무늬'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 이 가방에는 전통 문양이 그려져 있어요.
phrases.en: This bag has a traditional pattern drawn on it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문양이 가장 자주 어울리는 짝말로, 문화 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for 문양, used when talking about culture.

phrases.en: I carved a flower pattern into the pottery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그릇이나 돌처럼 단단한 것에 모양을 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making a design on something hard, like a bowl or stone.

phrases.en: This piece of clothing has a pretty pattern.
phrases.nuance_ko: '문양'과 비슷하지만 일상에서 더 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 문양 but more common in daily life.

explain_en: 문양 is the decorative shape repeated on clothes, dishes, or buildings. 무늬 is more common in daily talk, while 문양 appears more in talk about tradition, culture, and design. For stripes on clothes, 줄무늬 is more natural than 줄 문양.

t90.ax: This bowl has a flower pattern.

examples.en: The market has all sorts of things.
I've met every kind of person.

examples.ko: 별별 생각이 다 들어서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: All kinds of thoughts came to me, so I couldn't sleep.
All sorts of stories get posted on the internet.

examples.ko: 오늘은 별별 일이 다 생긴 하루였어요.
examples.en: Today was a day when all sorts of things happened.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 별별 음식을 다 팔아요.
examples.en: That shop sells every kind of food.

explain: '별별' 뒤에는 '사람', '일', '생각' 같은 말이 와서 '별별 사람', '별별 일'처럼 써요. 보통 '다'와 함께 '별별 게 다 있다'라고 하면서 놀라거나 어이없어하는 느낌을 담아요.

phrases.en: All sorts of things happened at work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상하지 못한 여러 가지 일이 있었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many unexpected kinds of things have happened.

phrases.example: 잠이 안 와서 별별 생각을 다 했어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't sleep and thought all sorts of things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이런저런 생각이 끝없이 떠오를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when all kinds of thoughts keep coming to mind.

phrases.example: 이 가게에는 별별 게 다 있어요.
phrases.en: This shop has every kind of thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종류가 아주 많아서 놀라는 느낌을 담은 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase expressing surprise at the sheer variety.

explain_en: It is followed by a noun like 사람, 일 or 생각, as in '별별 사람', '별별 일'. It often pairs with 다, as in '별별 게 다 있다', carrying a sense of surprise or disbelief.

t90.ax: I've met every kind of person.

examples.en: Effort and grades are not always proportional.
The pay is paid in proportion to the hours worked.

examples.ko: 속도가 두 배가 되면 거리도 두 배가 되어 서로 비례해요.
examples.en: If speed doubles, distance doubles too, so they are proportional.
The price will probably be proportional to the size.
I pay a fee in proportion to my usage.
The number of members is set in proportion to the population.

explain: 'A는 B에 비례한다'처럼 '~에/와 비례하다'로 써요. 한쪽이 커지면 다른 쪽도 같이 커지는 관계예요. 한쪽이 커질 때 다른 쪽이 줄어드는 관계는 '반비례하다'라고 해요. 수학, 과학, 경제 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The price is proportional to the size.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기가 커질수록 가격도 같이 커진다는 관계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that as the size gets bigger, the price goes up with it.

phrases.example: 키와 몸무게가 항상 비례하는 것은 아니에요.
phrases.en: Height and weight are not always in proportion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지가 꼭 같이 변하지는 않는다고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say gently that two things do not always change together.

phrases.en: Time and fee are in a proportional relationship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한쪽이 커지면 다른 쪽도 커지는 관계를 하나의 이름으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the relationship in which one thing grows as the other grows.

explain_en: Use it as '~에/와 비례하다' (A is proportional to B): when one grows, the other grows with it. If one grows while the other shrinks, it is '반비례하다'. It comes up often in math, science and economics.
